summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with a history of fibrosing mesenteritis, recurrent partial small bowel obstructions, and chronic GI dysmotility, was admitted for nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and diarrhea after attempting to advance from liquids to solids. Imaging confirmed an early partial small bowel obstruction without a transition point, likely precipitated by dietary advancement. She was managed conservatively with NPO status, G-tube suction, IV fluids, and anti-nausea medications. G-tube output decreased significantly, and she tolerated a gradual advancement to full liquids. She remained stable without suction for over 24 hours prior to discharge. Stool studies were negative for infection. She was discharged home in good condition on a full liquid diet with instructions to avoid solids for several days and follow up with GI. Pain was managed with oral morphine, and all home medications were continued with minor adjustments.
